subject.title: fix(agents): skip error classification for clean non-zero exits

question: What contract should distinguish an expected non-zero exec result from an ordinary failed command for channel warning purposes?
rationale: Exit code and `completed` process status alone cannot distinguish commands such as a no-match search from failed tests, builds, or Git operations; choosing the permanent signal and default is product policy.

options.title: Add explicit expected-exit semantics
options.body: Preserve non-zero-as-error by default and let the exec owner mark specific exit codes or outcomes as accepted before the generic warning classifier runs.

options.title: Suppress every completed non-zero exit
options.body: Adopt this PR's broad rule and accept that normally exited command failures will no longer trigger the fallback warning.

options.title: Keep the current policy
options.body: Continue warning for all non-zero exits and require commands expecting non-zero results to normalize them explicitly, such as through shell control flow.

recommendation.title: Add explicit expected-exit semantics
recommendation.body: Preserve non-zero-as-error by default and let the exec owner mark specific exit codes or outcomes as accepted before the generic warning classifier runs.
